'''Arie Rip''' (born 13 June 1941, in [[Kethel en Spaland]]) is a [[Dutch (people)|Dutch]] professor emeritus of Philosophy of Science and Technology.<ref>[https://people.utwente.nl/a.rip Profile of prof.dr. A. Rip (Arie) at the University of Twenthe]</ref>

== Career ==
During 1988–1989 he was the President of the international [[Society for Social Studies of Science]].
From 2000 until 2005 he was the head of WTMC, the Netherlands Graduate School of Science, Technology and Modern Culture. The WTMC is a formal collaboration of Dutch researchers studying the development of science, technology and modern culture. In 2006 Rip formally retired as the Professor of Philosophy of Science and Technology at the [[University of Twente]], a position he held since 1987.<ref>[https://www.nanowerk.com/news/newsid=10875.php "Ethical discussions concerning nanotechnology are often too futuristic"], Nanowerk, May 28, 2009</ref><ref>[https://www.nature.com/news/2008/081209/full/news.2008.1290.html "Fearing the fear of nanotechnology"], [[Nature (journal)|Nature]], December 9, 2008</ref> He has published extensively on various topics concerning the philosophy and sociology of scientific and technological developments, and on science and innovation policy.<ref>[http://www.euractiv.com/en/science/nanotech-risk-repeating-gm-food-fiasco/article-185862 "Nanotech at risk of repeating 'GM food fiasco'"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100208224544/http://www.euractiv.com/en/science/nanotech-risk-repeating-gm-food-fiasco/article-185862 |date=February 8, 2010 }}, Euractiv, September 29, 2009</ref> Rip has, for example, introduced the widely used Constructive Technology Assessment method.<ref>[http://www.nanowerk.com/news/newsid=368.php "The European Group on Ethics debated ethics of nanomedicine"], Nanowerk, March 23, 2006</ref><ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=CO_sAAAAMAAJ&q=%22Arie+Rip%22 Managing technology in society:] the approach of constructive technology assessment by Arie Rip, Thomas J. Misa and [[Johan Schot]], Pinter Publishers, 1995</ref><ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=0CL2JhDWvbsC&dq=%22Arie+Rip%22&pg=PA48 "Constructive Technology Assessment and Socio-Technical Scenarios"], ''The Yearbook of Nanotechnology in Society: Presenting Futures'' by Erik Fisher, Cynthia Selin and Jameson M. Wetmore, シュプリンガー・ジャパン株式会社, 2008</ref> Currently he is among others a Professor at the [[University of Stellenbosch]] in [[South Africa]].

Rip became chairman of the Society for the Study of Nanoscience and Emerging Technologies (S-NET) in 2008.<ref>[https://www.nanowerk.com/news/newsid=8367.php "New Society for the Study of Nanoscience and Emerging Technologies"], Nanowerk, November 25, 2008</ref>

In 2022 Rip received for his oeuvre the [[John Desmond Bernal Prize]] of the [[Society for Social Studies of Science]] (4S),<ref>[https://www.4sonline.org/prize/bernal-prize-2022-troy-duster-and-arie-rip/ "Bernal Prize 2022: Troy Duster and Arie Rip"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220622124307/https://www.4sonline.org/prize/bernal-prize-2022-troy-duster-and-arie-rip/ |date=2022-06-22 }} Archived August 2, 2022.</ref> which will be awarded to him in the second week of December, 2022, during a meeting of the Society at the [[Universidad Iberoamericana Puebla]] in [[San Andrés Cholula, Puebla]], [[Mexico]].

== Key publications ==
* Arie Rip (1981) ''Maatschappelijke Verantwoordelijkheid van Chemici'', PhD-thesis Leiden University, Leiden
* {{cite book | last1 = Law | first1 = John | last2 = Callon | first2 = Michel | last3 = Rip | first3 = Arie | author-link1 = John Law (sociologist) | author-link2 = Michel Callon | title = Mapping the dynamics of science and technology: sociology of science in the real world | publisher = Macmillan | location = Basingstoke | year = 1986 | isbn = 978-0-333-37223-4 }}
* Arie Rip (1994) The republic of science in the 1990s, ''Higher Education'', Vol. 28, pp.&nbsp;3–23
* Arie Rip, Thomas Misa, and [[Johan Schot]] (eds.) (1995) ''Managing Technology in Society: The Approach of Constructive Technology Assessment'', Pinter, London/New York.  {{ISBN|1-85567-340-1}}
* Johan Schot and Arie Rip (1996) The past and future of constructive technology assessment, ''Technological Forecasting and Social Change'', Vol 54, pp.&nbsp;251–268
* Arie Rip (1997) A cognitive approach to the relevance of science, ''Social Science Information'', Vol. 36 (4), pp.&nbsp;615–640
* Harro van Lente and Arie Rip (1998) The rise of membrane technology: from rhetorics to social reality, ''Social Studies of Science'', Vol. 28 (2), pp.&nbsp;221–254
* René Kemp, Arie Rip and Johan Schot (2001) Constructing transition paths through the management of niches, In: Garud, R., Karnoe, P. (Eds.), ''Path Dependence and Creation'', pp.&nbsp;269–302
* Arie Rip (2002) Science for the 21st century. In: Tindemans, P., [[Alex Verrijn Stuart|Verrijn-Stuart, A.]], Visser, R. (Eds.), ''The Future of Science and the Humanities'', Amsterdam University Press, Amsterdam, pp 99–148
* Stefan Kuhlmann and Arie Rip (2018) Next-Generation Innovation Policy and Grand Challenges ''Science and public policy'' Vol. 45 (4); pp 448–454; https://doi.org/10.1093/scipol/scy011
